items.title: United States
kv: Congress and the executive define federal statutes and policy; Treasury, FinCEN and OFAC govern financial-crime and sanctions functions; the federal banking agencies govern institution-specific bank and stablecoin capacities; the SEC and CFTC retain object- and activity-specific market authority; the Federal Reserve and Reserve Banks govern account access and central-bank payment services; states retain material licensing, trust, money-transmission and commercial-law roles.
Policy, legislation, rulemaking, chartering, licensing, account access, supervision, enforcement and transaction operation are separate federal and state capacities.

items.title: South Korea

items.title: Indonesia
kv: OJK took crypto and digital-financial-asset supervision from Bappebti on 10 January 2025 and now licenses exchanges, clearing/guarantee/settlement institutions, custodians and dealers under POJK 27/2024 as amended by POJK 23/2025. Bank Indonesia retains currency, payment-system, FX, QRIS, BI-FAST/RTGS and Digital Rupiah authority; PPATK and enforcement bodies retain AML and crime-response functions.
OJK trading or sandbox authority does not authorize a payment instrument or central-bank liability; BI payment authority does not license a crypto dealer.

items.title: European Union
kv: The Parliament and Council legislate, the Commission administers and proposes revisions, EBA and ESMA coordinate and exercise assigned functions, national competent authorities authorize and supervise exact entities, and the ECB and national central banks govern euro central-bank money and TARGET Services. EU legislation, agency advice, national authorization, prudential supervision and Eurosystem settlement authority are separate layers and clocks.

items.title: Kenya
kv: National Treasury owns the policy and regulations and chairs the coordination forum. CBK licenses wallets, virtual-asset payment processors and stablecoin issuers and owns currency, PSPs and KEPSS; CMA licenses exchanges, brokers, investment services, offerings and tokenisation. KRA owns tax; FRC and law-enforcement bodies retain AML and enforcement functions; courts and tribunals adjudicate. The National Treasury and CBK opened a separate draft National Payment System Policy and Bill on 21 September 2026; the policy anticipates implications for PSP licensing and remittance products that integrate tokenised or stablecoin arrangements, but it is a proposal, not current operating authority.
Policy, proposed payment-law reform, category-specific licensing, AML registration, tax reporting, PSP authorization, settlement operation, investigation and adjudication are different capacities.

The National Treasury and CBK opened a separate draft National Payment System Policy and Bill on 21 September 2026; the policy anticipates implications for PSP licensing and remittance products that integrate tokenised or stablecoin arrangements, but it is a proposal, not current operating authority.

catalog_context.title: Crypto around the world: many licenses, no proven cross-border use
catalog_context.answer: Across 22 jurisdictions, we found no verified cross-border payment route that depends on crypto from end to end. The token layer still settles through ordinary banks and national payment systems.
